parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Section four. You will hear part of a lecture about the art and design of New Zealand's Maori people. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today's lecture will be an introduction to the art and design of the Maori people who lived in New Zealand before Europeans arrived. So let's start and outline the general development of Maori arts.

Now, as you know, Maori originally migrated to New Zealand from the Pacific Islands in about the year nine hundred. And from then until around eleven hundred, their arts changed little. But during the next period, from eleven hundred to sixteen fifty, a distinct style emerged as they became more familiar with the local resources. Not the plants, which were basically similar, but the sort of stone found here was different from the corals of the Pacific Islands. The next stage, from sixteen fifty to eighteen hundred, was the high point of Maori art and design. By this time, a high level of local artistry had evolved, a point illustrated by the fact that within the wider community, artists now enjoyed greater status than at any time before or since in society. Then, with the coming of Europeans in about eighteen hundred, the next fifty years, until eighteen fifty, obviously saw numerous changes for Maori. In terms of art and design, the arrival of steel made little difference as sophisticated tools were already being manufactured. And what's quite clear is that carved patterns became more elaborate once paints were introduced by the Europeans. And these quickly replaced the natural colors that had been filled the carvings until then. Okay, let's look next at some particular types of art and design. So first, weaving. Quite clean vases were woven from vegetable fibers in numerous sizes and served all manner of routine functions. But much the most important was for storage, especially for food items. Then there were other baskets made with greater craftsmanship, the designs more intricate, often highly colored and decorative, which typically played the role of gifts. So turning next to plaiting. Rope was made by plaiting together three or more strands of fiber, and it was used frequently on sailing canoes. Another item to use plaited rope was the mooker, a T-shaped stick with a thin rope attached to it. It was commonly used for hunting. A bird would perch on the stick, and the rope was then twisted around its legs. Now, kites were also made using these techniques, a light cladded string being attached to a finely woven vine. Kites were popular with children who flew them as a sport. But they also had more serious functions, one of which was important in warfare. When kites were sometimes used on a prominent place like a hilltop to send a signal to another village.

Now, turning now to tattooing and carving. Tattoos were common on both men and women, though the significance was not quite the same. A woman was usually tattooed when she reached maturity, and this was nearly always applied to her face, the tattoos being highly prized. Men were more heavily tattooed, particularly on their arms and legs, though the patterns are considered to be more decorative. Oh, and carving. This was used to produce many functional items, things like fish hooks. But then there were other carved designs, for example, those sometimes found on the entrance gateway to a village that were intended to maintain security. Not from the enemy, that was man's work, but things like storms, perhaps. Within the village, the practice developed of carving vertical posts so as to keep a record of those who had gone before. The posts, often located outside a home, were seen as a means for people to remember and celebrate the lives of their ancestors on a regular basis. So, um, what conclusions can we draw? Well, the first thing is that-

That is the end of part four. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to part four.

analyses.content: 录音明确指出“这里的 stone（石头）种类与太平洋岛屿的珊瑚不同”，直接对应了题目中的 not the same as the corals。
你可能会在听到 plants 时想填入，但录音随后用 basically similar 否定了植物的差异，真正不同的是 stone。

But during the next period, from eleven hundred to sixteen fifty, a distinct style emerged as they became more familiar with the local resources. Not the plants, which were basically similar, but the sort of stone found here was different from the corals of the Pacific Islands.
录音中提到艺术家们“enjoyed greater status（享有更高的地位）”，对应了题目的 rise in the status。
这句话相对较长，你可能会被前半句的 local artistry 分散注意力，需要紧盯题目中关于 artists 发生了什么变化来抓取核心名词 status。

The next stage, from sixteen fifty to eighteen hundred, was the high point of Maori art and design. By this time, a high level of local artistry had evolved, a point illustrated by the fact that within the wider community, artists now enjoyed greater status than at any time before or since in society.
录音说明“一旦欧洲人引入了 paints（颜料），雕刻图案就变得更加 elaborate（复杂）”，elaborate 直接同义替换了题目里的 intricate。
你可能会听到前面的 steel 或者后面的 Europeans 并想填入，但录音特意强调钢的到来“made little difference（几乎没有影响）”，而欧洲人是引入者，真正促使图案变复杂的事物是 paints。

In terms of art and design, the arrival of steel made little difference as sophisticated tools were already being manufactured. And what's quite clear is that carved patterns became more elaborate once paints were introduced by the Europeans. And these quickly replaced the natural colors that had been filled the carvings until then.
录音提到这种植物纤维做的花瓶最重要（most important）的用途是 for storage（用于储存），尤其是针对食物（food items），完全契合题目。
你可能会听到前面的 routine functions 就着急写答案，但题目明确限定了与 food 相关的用途，必须往后听到 storage 才能填。
Quite clean vases were woven from vegetable fibers in numerous sizes and served all manner of routine functions. But much the most important was for storage, especially for food items.
录音指出这些制作精美的篮子通常扮演 gifts（礼物）的角色（played the role of），对应题目的 functioned as。
这个句子中间塞入了大量的修饰词（intricate, colored, decorative），很容易让你跟丢逻辑，要耐心等到句子末尾抓取核心结论名词 gifts。
Then there were other baskets made with greater craftsmanship, the designs more intricate, often highly colored and decorative, which typically played the role of gifts.
录音直接给出了这种叫 mooker 的工具的用途，即 commonly used for hunting（通常用于打猎）。
你可能会被前面的 stick 或者 rope 干扰，但题目问的是“is used for（用来做什么）”，必须抓取表示具体行为的名词 hunting。

Another item to use plaited rope was the mooker, a T-shaped stick with a thin rope attached to it. It was commonly used for hunting. A bird would perch on the stick, and the rope was then twisted around its legs.
录音在讲述风筝在战争中的作用时，明确说它被用来 send a signal（发送信号），send 对应了题目中的 deliver。
你可能会把听到的 hilltop 直接填上，但从句子结构 deliver a ______ 来看，传递“山顶”不符合逻辑，传递 signal（信号）才是正确语义。
But they also had more serious functions, one of which was important in warfare. When kites were sometimes used on a prominent place like a hilltop to send a signal to another village.
录音说明当女性成熟时，纹身几乎总是 applied to her face（涂在脸上），这对应了题目的 placed on the face。
如果你没有听准性别主语，很容易将紧接着后面讲男性的纹身部位 arms 或者 legs 填入，必须牢牢记住题目问的是 women。

Tattoos were common on both men and women, though the significance was not quite the same. A woman was usually tattooed when she reached maturity, and this was nearly always applied to her face, the tattoos being highly prized. Men were more heavily tattooed, particularly on their arms and legs, though the patterns are considered to be more decorative.
录音提到村庄入口的雕刻旨在维持安全，防范的不是敌人，而是像 storms（风暴）这样的事情。
录音故意用 enemy 设下了一个陷阱，如果你漏听了前面的否定词 Not，就会中招填错。

But then there were other carved designs, for example, those sometimes found on the entrance gateway to a village that were intended to maintain security. Not from the enemy, that was man's work, but things like storms, perhaps.
录音指出这些柱子是人们 remember and celebrate（纪念和庆祝）他们 ancestors（祖先）的一种方式，这与题目中的 memorial for 意思一致。
你可能会在听到上一句的 those who had gone before（先人）时就想写，但这超出了一个单词的字数限制，只有耐心听到紧接着的名词 ancestors 才能得出符合要求的最终答案。

Within the village, the practice developed of carving vertical posts so as to keep a record of those who had gone before. The posts, often located outside a home, were seen as a means for people to remember and celebrate the lives of their ancestors on a regular basis.
